findings.summary: Census is limited by one long recognition sequence: OCR accounts for 89.2% of a 29.78 s call. Most GPUs finish before the tail.
observations: Current frozen configuration: one warm-up, three ordinary measured calls, and a separate instrumented full-PDF call. Median OCR is 26.59 s; median embedding is 3.09 s.
A page-5 region generates 3,252 tokens. Its page runs after page 1 on layout worker 0, so some recognition work starts late. The text finishes with EOS and matches the frozen reference.
Mean OCR-window GPU busy for GPUs 0–3 is [92.8, 6.8, 6.9, 15.3]%; sample counts are [79, 79, 80, 80]. This is a different load pattern from the short NACA document.
OCR-window mean running requests per server are [1.01, 0.16, 0.1, 0.42]. Fractions of observations with no running requests are [0.114, 0.94, 0.948, 0.843].

All four bounded vLLM traces were captured, and the instrumented full output passes the frozen-reference check. The trace covers early iterations; GPU/request telemetry covers the complete measured OCR stages.
Idle recognizers near the end show workload imbalance. Busy/power/clock measurements do not establish achieved peak compute or memory-bandwidth saturation.
findings.next_step: First reduce embedding time; then test dynamic page assignment and a wider region submission window without changing OCR content.
findings.optimization: Use available layout workers for waiting pages sooner, and examine whether per-page submission barriers leave recognition work queued outside vLLM. A long autoregressive sequence remains a separate limit.
